subject: botany
question_text: Explain in brief the scope of Botany in relation to agriculture, horticulture and medicine.

verification.note: Sourced from the Telangana Junior Fastrack botany guide, Chapter 3 'Science of Plants' (book pp.5-6). The botany book prints NO star ranks and NO year citations, so stars=0 and appearances=[] record absence of signal, not measured frequency. Only ONE botany source is held — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper exists in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for botany: 'unverified' means never yet checkable against a second source, not checked-and-clean. The 1+2+1 split follows the weight of the book's own answer (two agriculture points, three horticulture points, one medicine point) and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book spells 'Belladona'; the card writes Belladonna.

steps.label: Scope in agriculture
lines: Development of hybrid varieties in crop
plants such as rice and wheat.
steps.why: Botany reaches farming in two ways: plant breeding (hybrid varieties give better yield) and plant nutrition (recognising and correcting mineral deficiencies).
common_mistakes: Writing 'better crops' with no named example — rice and wheat make the point concrete.
Mixing horticulture points (ripening, cuttings) into the agriculture paragraph.
steps.memory_tip: Farm gains come in two ways: better seed (hybrids) and better feeding (minerals).
steps.margin_note: Two points under a clear agriculture heading.

steps.label: Scope in horticulture
lines: Leafy vegetables such as spinach are kept
Fruits such as apple and banana are
Stem cuttings are rooted for vegetative
steps.why: Horticulture applies plant knowledge after harvest and in the garden: keeping produce fresh, ripening fruit when needed, and multiplying plants from cuttings.
common_mistakes: Writing only one horticulture point — this part carries the most content, so give all three.
Writing seeds instead of stem cuttings for vegetative propagation — vegetative means without seeds.
steps.memory_tip: Three horticulture verbs in order: keep (shelf life), ripen (fruits), root (cuttings).
steps.margin_note: Three points; this heading carries two of the four marks.

steps.label: Scope in medicine
lines: The medicinal values of plants such as Neem,
Datura, Ocimum, Belladonna and Aloe are used

lines.text: Botany serves agriculture, horticulture and medicine.

steps.why: The medicine part rests on named medicinal plants — their known medicinal values are the starting material for developing medicines, including in Ayurvedic pharmacies.
common_mistakes: Listing no plant names — at least two of Neem, Datura, Ocimum, Belladonna, Aloe are expected.
Claiming the plants cure named diseases — state only that their medicinal values are used to develop medicines.
steps.memory_tip: Five medicinal plants to list: Neem, Datura, Ocimum, Belladonna, Aloe.
steps.margin_note: One point with plant names, then the boxed closing line.

insider_note: Answer under three labelled headings in the question's own order; a single unlabelled paragraph makes the examiner search for the three parts and often costs a mark.
